statement: The retrieved literature establishes that user temporal intent is heterogeneous and requires inference - temporal query profiling is defined as inferring when a query is directed in time, and prior work studied the prevalence of different temporal orientations of user queries across past, future and present - and that legal RAG systems do cite real documents anachronistically. It reports no rate, however, for how often legal information-seeking questions are date-constrained or target a superseded legal state, and the temporal-orientation prevalence study is cited without figures.

evidence.quote: Joho et al. (2013) studied the prevalence of different temporal orientations of user queries, and the strategies user apply to find temporally relevant content from the past, future or present.
inferring when the query is directed in time rather than analyzing any specific document
RAG-augmented legal AI tends instead to cite real documents in ways that are anachronistic
